entries.agent_prompt:
You are helping me prepare a Bifrost human-authentication cutover.
You can reach my Bifrost deployment configuration, API/MCP ingress configuration, and a shell with access to the running deployment.
1. Inspect the deployment and identify every API replica, MCP endpoint, and WebSocket route that must stop serving during maintenance.
2. Propose the exact maintenance plan, including how to block and drain traffic, apply the release, verify a homogeneous API and MCP fleet on the selected release, and re-enable service. Include supported SDK updates for deployed V2 Apps; obtain original source for redeployment if retained source is unavailable, and verify the activated SDK provenance before reopening each App. Explain the browser, CLI, and MCP reauthentication step, and wait for my confirmation.
3. After I confirm, apply the plan and verify login/MFA, a normal request, refresh rotation, logout or revoke-all, MCP reconnect, and WebSocket reconnect.
Do not change anything unrelated, and stop if the deployment does not match the plan.
entries.markdown: Self-hosted administrators: schedule maintenance for this upgrade. Block and drain API, MCP, and WebSocket traffic, then verify every serving API and MCP endpoint runs the new build. Update deployed V2 App SDKs before reopening those Apps. Everyone must sign in again in browsers, the CLI, and MCP clients. Ordinary rolling deployment and rollback below this authentication version are unsupported. The runtime legacy bridge remains supported.
entries.title: Required: Plan an Authentication Maintenance Cutover

entries.agent_prompt:
You are helping me clean up my Bifrost Kubernetes deployment after scaling and isolation moved to Settings.
You can reach my Bifrost Kubernetes manifests or GitOps repository and kubectl access to the Bifrost namespace.
1. Ask me whether I may still roll back to the previous Bifrost release. If I may, stop.
2. Read the API startup log for the warnings that name environment variables no longer read or to be renamed, and check that Settings → Kubernetes → Scaling & Isolation lists the same variables.
3. Find where each of them is set in my manifests (ConfigMaps, Secrets, Deployment env).
4. Propose the exact changes and wait for my confirmation: remove each variable that is no longer read, and rename each BIFROST_KUBERNETES_BUILD_ variable that is still read to its BIFROST_KUBERNETES_JOB_ name, or remove it if it only repeats what the API pod already uses.
5. Apply them, roll out the API, then verify that the startup log has no such warnings, the Settings notice is empty, and a test workflow run succeeds.
Do not change anything unrelated, and stop if anything does not match what you expect.
entries.markdown:
On Kubernetes, worker scaling and build isolation are now set in Settings → Kubernetes → Scaling & Isolation, and changes apply without a restart. On first start, Bifrost copies your current environment values there and lists the variables you can then remove. Isolated builds also get a larger pod when they need more memory.

[Open Scaling & Isolation](/settings/kubernetes-executions)
entries.title: Scaling and Isolation Move to Settings

entries.agent_prompt:
You are helping me upgrade my Bifrost install to the unified worker runtime.
You can reach my Bifrost deployment files (docker-compose.yml or Kubernetes manifests) and a shell with docker or kubectl access to it.
1. Find how Bifrost is deployed and report what applies:
   - the scheduler and worker services or Deployments, with their replicas and memory limits;
   - any rabbitmq service or Deployment, and any KEDA ScaledObject or TriggerAuthentication for Bifrost;
   - these retired environment variables, if set: BIFROST_RABBITMQ_URL, BIFROST_MAX_CONCURRENCY, BIFROST_MAX_WORKERS, BIFROST_MAX_SERVICE_WORKERS.
   - Also list any variable that the API's startup log names as no longer read.
2. If RabbitMQ is still running, check the API logs for "Drained work queued by an earlier release". If that line is missing, stop and tell me.
3. Propose the exact changes and wait for my confirmation:
   - Docker Compose: one worker service with 2 replicas and a 2 GB memory limit each, as in the current Bifrost docker-compose.yml; remove the scheduler and rabbitmq services; then run docker compose up -d --remove-orphans.
   - Kubernetes: apply the new base manifests; once the bifrost-worker and bifrost-scheduler pods are gone, delete those Deployments; delete the rabbitmq Deployment and Service and any Bifrost KEDA ScaledObject and TriggerAuthentication.
   - Remove the retired environment variables listed above.
4. Apply them, then verify that the API's /health/ready check passes and a test workflow run succeeds.
Do not change anything unrelated, and stop if anything does not match what you expect.
entries.markdown:
The scheduler and worker now run one executor that handles every job type, so an unchanged scheduler works as a second worker. RabbitMQ and KEDA are no longer used; remove them once the API logs that it drained. We recommend 2 GB per worker for most high-memory jobs and agent headroom; larger app builds may need more.

[Sizing Guide](https://github.com/gobifrost/bifrost/blob/main/docs/runbooks/kubernetes-worker-deployment.md#resource-sizing)
entries.title: Recommended: Upgrade to the Unified Worker

entries.markdown:
On Kubernetes, the API starts worker Jobs as work arrives and drains them when idle, keeping one warm for instant runs and up to six by default. After an upgrade, workers on the old build are replaced once a new one is ready, and their runs finish first. Set the range in Settings → Kubernetes.

[Open Diagnostics](/diagnostics)
entries.title: Workers Scale on Demand in Kubernetes

assets.alt: A workflow's Execution settings with its learned Memory Request
assets.caption: A workflow requests the memory its recent runs used, unless you set one.

entries.markdown:
Workers now take work by memory, not fixed slots. Each workflow learns its memory use, or set a Memory Request in its settings. A run too large for a standard worker gets a larger one on Kubernetes; work no worker can hold fails at once. Max worker and concurrency settings are now ignored.

[Open Workflows](/workflows)

![A workflow's Execution settings with its learned Memory Request](assets/56853509-1ca2-4e7f-8c7d-dc84c1521837/memory-request.png)
entries.title: Workflows Run by Memory, Not Slots

entries.markdown:
Automatic mode for agents coordinates chat and background jobs in one conversation using approved specialist tools and optional subagents; [CodeMode](https://blog.cloudflare.com/code-mode-mcp/) batches calls and filters intermediate results. Our testing showed 41% lower recorded cost and 54% lower median runtime versus earlier Automatic; Delegated remains the default.

[Enable Automatic in AI Behavior Settings](/settings/ai-chat)
entries.title: Automatic Agent Execution

entries.markdown: Workflows can now move files within a location, such as a Solution's `docs`, with `files.move`, or up to 500 at a time with `files.move_many`. Files are copied on the server, keep their metadata, and pick up access from their new path. The CLI adds `bifrost files move`.
entries.title: Move Files in a Location

entries.markdown:
Privileged users can select **Impersonate** on a user's profile to work in their session across browser tabs. A banner identifies the active session and provides **Exit**. Audit records retain the original operator's identity.

[Open Users](/users)
entries.title: Impersonate a User

entries.markdown:
Zero Trust Automation checks each run against the run user's current roles and organization reach. Full Access adds every permission within that reach; Declared Permissions adds only the workflow's configured permissions. A run identity records who acts, while agents and inline scripts add no workflow powers. Before upgrading, drain queued and active runs and update the API and workers together. Review runs refused for a missing run user or acting user before restarting them under a valid identity. Reapprove affected Solution permission requests.

[Open Access Checks](/audit/access-checks)
entries.title: Zero Trust Automation Checks Roles and Reach

entries.markdown:
Changing privileged role permissions requires Read and Write Privileged Access. Administrators can read and dismiss admin notifications while personal notifications stay with their owner.

[Open Roles](/roles)
entries.title: Scope Role Edits and Notification Access

assets.alt: Auditing with grouped checks and a compact record selector.

entries.markdown:
Switch between Activity and Access Checks on the Auditing page. Group checks by time, then open a summary to inspect individual records and compare Then with Now. New installs retain audits for one year, including 30 days in the database.

[Open Access Checks](/audit/access-checks)

![Auditing with grouped checks and a compact record selector.](assets/ac0cc537-02ca-4357-849f-3e8ece879782/access-checks.png)

entries.markdown:
Agents can now run as another user from the SDK with `run_as`, like workflows. Both need Impersonate Users in that user's organization instead of Platform Admin, and Platform Admins keep it. Run As shows on the agent run, and Access Checks records each impersonation.

[Open Roles](/roles) · [Open Access Checks](/audit/access-checks)
entries.title: Run Agents as Another User

entries.markdown:
Every admin-only power now has a named permission. Access Checks records, report-only, when someone uses one their roles don't grant. New: Run Agents, Use AI, Read AI Model Information, Impersonate Users, Read and Write Privileged Access, Read Basic views. Four are renamed. Nobody's access changes.

[Open Access Checks](/audit/access-checks) · [Open Roles](/roles)
entries.title: Named Permissions in Access Checks

entries.markdown:
**CLI/SDK users:** upgrade to 1.4.2 or later with the platform. Versions through 1.4.1 cannot parse the new execution response. Refresh external MCP clients for the renamed `bifrost_<noun>_<verb>` tools. The interactive local runner is removed; direct workflow runs remain. App management now requires Platform Admin.

[Open MCP Settings](/settings/mcp)
entries.title: Update the CLI and MCP Clients

other_changes.title: Agent runs and chat messages run in separate worker processes, so a busy or memory-full API no longer delays or blocks them.
Agent runs and chat messages start immediately again, without waiting for the worker to load the agent runtime.
App build memory failures now explain the cause and give local-build or container-memory recovery guidance.
App lists and Integration controls now reflect the access already enforced when opening or updating a resource. Home organization names display consistently.
App SDK updates no longer fail on npm lockfile metadata or unrelated Solution entity definitions.
Apply custom logos consistently across Solutions, forms, and integrations.
Apply organization permissions to live table subscriptions.
Apps receive workflow completion before follow-up bookkeeping.
Audit failed sign-ins.
Audit permission-rule changes.
Avoid duplicate sign-in redirects when a session expires.
Chat shows current context usage and cached input beside the model selector.
CLI browser login keeps waiting through temporary throttling and stops when its device code expires.
CLI sign-in fills in your device code and asks you to confirm the account and access before connecting.
CLI workflow execution exits correctly when a run finishes before log streaming connects.
Concurrent synchronous workflow calls no longer hold database connections while waiting for execution results.
Concurrent table-document merges preserve changes to different fields instead of silently overwriting an earlier writer.
Dashboard charts keep working after opening and closing the code editor.
Deleted integration names can be reused as clean new connections without reviving their previous settings.
Deleting an integration now stops its OAuth token refreshes and the repeated refresh-failed alerts.
Developer settings now links to the current external SDK documentation.
Diagnostics labels API control replicas as Control, not Job Runner; only executors that run jobs show as Job Runner.
Event source events scroll on desktop, and the webhook URL is a compact copy button.
Execution logs survive completion races and database rollbacks.
Find global Solutions when working inside an organization.
Full Access workflows can again use tables and files whose policies admit platform admins, even when the person running them is not one.
Git sync rejects unknown manifest fields and duplicate keys before changing workspace entities or publishing source.
GitHub token validation now shows the GitHub HTTP status and error reason in Settings.
Include the latest README in Solution exports.
Inline apps no longer lose table data or saves when the sign-in session lapses; they renew the session and retry.
integrations.list_mappings lists every mapping you can see again, whatever scope it is passed, so callers using "global" or the provider organization see their customers.
Keep a replacement worker warm before a worker reaches its lifetime limit.
Keep an active human Platform Admin and prevent external accounts from holding privileged roles. Deleting a user cancels their unstarted workflow runs.
Keep existing workers available while replacements finish starting.
Keep idle worker control subscriptions connected and identify dependencies that fail readiness checks.
Keep streaming responses visible when a new conversation is saved.
Keep workflow services connected after credentials renew.
Let embedded apps view the workflow runs they started.
Local previews stop retrying rejected logins and can reconnect after a new login; refused worker connections no longer produce duplicate-close errors.
Local Solution previews use the signed-in user's permissions to access sealed install data. Unresolved table queries report an error instead of appearing empty.

MCP OAuth setup creates independent providers, and a migration removes credentials left behind by deleted integrations. API clients must use inline OAuth configuration instead of an existing provider ID; installations with shared MCP credentials must reconnect before upgrading.
On Kubernetes, an upgrade now always replaces worker Jobs that are still running the previous version.
On Kubernetes, the cluster drops the extra node a deploy adds once the worker on it is idle, without interrupting any running job.
Open the Bifrost YouTube channel from the header Help menu.
Platform admins can again refresh, deep-link and stay on an App that belongs to a client organization.
Platform Admins can edit their own role assignments and explicitly grant or remove Secrets Reader.
Platform Admins opening a customer’s App now use that customer’s tables, files, and workflow context.
Redis listeners release their connections even when unsubscribe cleanup fails.
Reduce API memory retained after large responses.
Reduce repeated database work when workflows, services, and agents authenticate SDK requests.
Reduced API memory use while retaining existing workflows, jobs, and MCP access.
Reduced repeated database work when workflows and agents authenticate SDK calls.
Remote runners preserve active workflow sessions when reconnecting.
Restore authorized users' workflow and data access from sealed Solution apps without rebuilding their apps.
Restore standard users’ ability to open authorized Apps and show readable App-loading errors.
Restore workflows' ability to list every integration mapping their roles reach, and keep mapping lookups by entity within that reach.
Restrict system-account roles and unavailable agent tools.
Retry event deliveries with a fresh timeout.
Save changes reliably before requests complete.
Save organization settings before an integration is mapped.
Scoped SDK operations read only the Solution metadata needed to check access.
SDK updates can rebuild retained Solution sources with identical duplicate files, and valid App dependency trees no longer crash the build installer.
SDK updates work for Apps captured into a Solution.
Show consistent totals when listing service attempts.
Show only pending workflows in queue positions and clearly reject invalid execution status filters.
Show the actual error when OAuth renewal fails.
Solution CLI prebuilds now retain the SDK provenance used to compile V2 Apps.
Solution deployments refresh source caches faster and report publication progress.
Solution deployments spend less time refreshing source caches.
Solution deploys and Git updates use isolated build capacity when it is enabled.
Solution details now show the same managed-entity counts as the Solution list.
Solution installs and deploys show the npm or Vite error when an app build fails, instead of pointing to server logs.
Solution workflows can batch-write their global tables while preserving the executing organization.
Stop app builds when they are cancelled.
The audit retention setting shows the real 30-day default while it loads, and an app's SDK update status no longer jumps back to queued after the update has started.
The sidebar and header stay in place while a page loads, instead of the whole workspace flashing to a loading screen.
Webhook subscribers can verify provider signatures using the original request bytes, including queued deliveries and retries.
Workers now report their own build version and handle interrupted enrollment and startup failures correctly.
Workers use less memory while idle and preserve running workflows through API restarts.
Workflow and service logs mask credential-bearing HTTP headers while retaining user DEBUG messages.
Workflow authoring rejects unsupported decorator settings, and Solution imports reject invalid manifests.
Workflow control and notifications reuse the API Redis pool, avoiding repeated TLS setup on each operation.
Workflow policy logging avoids repeated database reads, and full worker pools can update while preserving warm capacity.
Workflow results containing dates, UUIDs, and decimals complete correctly on thin workers, including after controller ownership loss.
Workflow tool updates use less memory and rebuild faster.
Workflow tools keep a single category prefix. Automatic agents favor tools in the current conversation and expose one optional subagent interface.
Workflows continue through queue-display outages, and event delivery status follows the actual workflow or agent run.
Workflows that use a Global table by name from an organization read and write that table again instead of creating a private copy.
